weather.headline: Flood Warning issued September 19 at 10:59AM EDT until September 25 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...Ohio...

Wabash River near Bluffton IN affecting Wells County.

Saint Marys River at St. Mary's River near Fort Wayne affecting
Allen IN County.

Saint Marys River near Decatur affecting Allen IN, Adams and Van
Wert Counties.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...

Wabash River near Linn Grove affecting Wells and Adams Counties.

For the Wabash River...including Linn Grove, Bluffton IN, Wabash,
Logansport...Moderate flooding is forecast.
For the Saint Marys River...including Decatur, St. Mary's River near
Fort Wayne...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River near Bluffton IN.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Flooding begins to affect residential areas
in northern Bluffton. Low areas near the wastewater treatment plant
begin to flood. Portions of Elm Grove Road and County Road 450
begin to flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 14.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 9.7 feet Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Detailed river forecasts and additional information can be found at
www.weather.gov/iwx under Rivers and Lakes.

This statement will be updated within the next 12 to 24 hours.

events.title: There Is No Genocide in Gaza, and Civilian Deaths or Widespread Destruction Alone Do Not Prove Otherwise
events.description: When discussing the war in Gaza, one of the most frequent and serious allegations leveled against Israel is that it is committing genocide. Yet genocide is not simply another word for a brutal war, extensive destruction, or a tragically high civilian death toll. It is a narrowly defined crime under international law that requires very specific elements, most importantly the intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a protected group as such. Critics of Israel routinely point to civilian casualties or destruction in Gaza as though these facts alone establish genocidal intent, but they do not. This discussion will be divided into several sections: The Israel-Palestine Conflict, Palestinian Terrorist Organizations, Accusations of Stealing Land, October 7th, Intent, Rhetoric, The Genocide Convention, and Conclusion. The Israel-Palestine Conflict The Gaza war, like every war in the Israel–Palestine conflict, did not emerge from a vacuum. The pivotal starting point for the modern conflict is 1947, when the United Nations adopted Resolution 181, proposing the partition of Mandatory Palestine into independent Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem under international administration. Jewish leaders accepted partition, while Palestinian leaders and the surrounding Arab states rejected it. Rather than accept the creation of a Jewish state alongside an Arab one, Arab forces figured they outnumbered the Jews 40 million to 700,000, and they could just kill the Jews and take it all. When that failed spectacularly and resulted in what Palestinians remember as the “Nakba,” that would be the earliest starting point for the current conflict. Palestinians continued to reject generous proposals for a peaceful resolution to the conflict, most notably and most recently the Olmert Proposal in 2008. Any reasonable person could easily conclude, after reviewing these proposals and the history, that Palestinians have no evidence of any desire for peace. That is a critical factor that shapes Israeli and Jewish opinion, especially today. Palestinian Terrorist Organizations For the purpose of discussing the Gaza war, I will focus on the two most prominent terrorist organizations in Gaza, Hamas and the Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Both of these are terrorist organizations that consistently commit war crimes and crimes against humanity. Both of these organizations use Palestinian civilians as human shields, and both of these organizations employ the use of hostage taking to achieve political objectives. In regards to Hamas, who is the democratically elected governing body of Gaza. They have consistently embedded their military infrastructure in schools, hospitals, religious sites, historical sites, UN facilities, civilian housing, and other civilian infrastructure. They have poured billions of dollars of foreign aid into developing this terror network deeply within the civilian population. Hamas’s deliberate strategy is to ensure that they cannot be militarily targeted without massive devastation to Palestinian infrastructure and the population. Accusations of Stealing Land A frequent argument critics of Israel bring up when arguing against Israel is that Israel’s goal during war is to steal or acquire land. However, this is easily disproven given the fact that Israel has returned land for peace numerous times. Israel gave Jordan and Egypt control of Gaza and the West Bank in exchange for peace after the Arab Israeli War in 1948. Israel returned the Sinai in exchange for peace after the Six-Day War in 1982. Israel withdrew all the settlers from Gaza in 2005 in an attempt to achieve peace. Israel on many occasions has demonstrated it prioritizes peace over land acquisition. The only side that actually never offered peace was the Palestinians. October 7th On October 7th, Hamas launched a savage invasion of Israel, sending thousands of armed terrorists across the border while simultaneously firing thousands of missiles into the Jewish state. Israeli communities were overrun, civilians were murdered in cold blood and abducted, and Israel was forced into a war it did not initiate. The following day, Hezbollah opened a second front from Lebanon, beginning sustained drone and missile attacks against northern Israel in declared support of Hamas. Within hours of the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust, Israel was confronting coordinated threats from multiple fronts while fighting to defend its citizens and secure the return of its hostages. This was not just a terrorist attack, but a declaration of war by the democratically elected governing body of Gaza, Hamas. During this barbaric day, Israeli civilians were murdered in cold blood, entire communities were massacred, children were kidnapped and dragged into Gaza, and Jews were slaughtered in the largest single-day massacre of Jews since the Holocaust. events.description: ...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Wisconsin...Illinois... Fox River Lower Near New Munster affecting Kenosha and Lake Counties. Root River Canal At Raymond affecting Racine County. .Two rivers in southeast Wisconsin remain in flood stage following recent rains of 3.5 to 4.5 inches. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Fox River Lower near New Munster. * WHEN...Until late Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Water is up to the first floor levels of some homes in the Town of Wheatland, Silver Lake and Village of Salem Lakes area along Riverside Drive and Shorewood Drive. Hoosier Creek Rd floods. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 9:00 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 11.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 9:00 PM CDT Sunday was 11.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 11.9 feet early tomorrow afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late Wednesday evening. - Flood stage is 11.0 feet. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.7 feet on 05/10/2019. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Lake, IL; Kenosha, WI

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued September 20 at 9:57PM CDT until September 24 at 5:00AM CDT by NWS Milwaukee/Sullivan WI
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Wisconsin...Illinois...

Fox River Lower Near New Munster affecting Kenosha and Lake
Counties.

Root River Canal At Raymond affecting Racine County.

.Two rivers in southeast Wisconsin remain in flood stage following
recent rains of 3.5 to 4.5 inches.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Fox River Lower near New Munster.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Water is up to the first floor levels of
some homes in the Town of Wheatland, Silver Lake and Village of

Creek Rd floods.

- At 9:00 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 11.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 11.9 feet
early tomorrow afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage
late Wednesday evening.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.7
feet on 05/10/2019.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Much of south-central New Mexico and Far West Texas, including El Paso, Las Cruces, and the Mesilla Valley. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos, rivers, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded, resulting in road closures. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An early season back door cold front will interact with a late season plume of deep monsoonal moisture, bringing several rounds of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. - A broad swath of moderate to locally heavy rainfall is likely to affect most of the Watch area between late Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday evening, with typical, scattered monsoon season flood impacts. However, there is increasing potential for a narrow band of repeated thunderstorms which will result in particularly heavy rainfall amounts, possibly exceeding 3 inches in a 6 to 12 hour period, resulting in higher-end impacts. Forecast models currently favor placing the focus for heaviest rainfall over the Mesilla Valley and El Paso. But forecasts this far out, especially when dealing with thunderstorms, are simply not accurate enough to precisely tell yet where exactly this area of heaviest rainfall will set up. It could just as easily shift west or east and avoid the more populated corridor. - http://www.weather.gov/ElPaso

weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Much of south-central New Mexico and Far West Texas,
including El Paso, Las Cruces, and the Mesilla Valley.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos,
rivers, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded, resulting in road closures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An early season back door cold front will interact with a late
season plume of deep monsoonal moisture, bringing several rounds
of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday
afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may
tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end
precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest
rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday
morning.
- A broad swath of moderate to locally heavy rainfall is likely to
affect most of the Watch area between late Tuesday afternoon and
Wednesday evening, with typical, scattered monsoon season flood
impacts. However, there is increasing potential for a narrow band
of repeated thunderstorms which will result in particularly heavy
rainfall amounts, possibly exceeding 3 inches in a 6 to 12 hour
period, resulting in higher-end impacts. Forecast models
currently favor placing the focus for heaviest rainfall over the
Mesilla Valley and El Paso. But forecasts this far out,
especially when dealing with thunderstorms, are simply not
accurate enough to precisely tell yet where exactly this area of
heaviest rainfall will set up. It could just as easily shift west
or east and avoid the more populated corridor.
- http://www.weather.gov/ElPaso
weather.instruction:
The forecast will be fine-tuned and will evolve over time. You should
monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood Warnings
Tuesday afternoon and evening. The Wednesday morning commute may also
be impacted. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

rivers and streams in the watch area should monitor the latest

forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

Indiana...

Wabash River near Bluffton IN affecting Wells County.

Wabash River near Linn Grove affecting Adams and Wells Counties.

For the Wabash River...including Linn Grove, Bluffton IN...Minor
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Wabash River near Linn Grove.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Secondary roads are blocked. Roads near the
east side of Geneva begin to flood. Some evacuations may be
required and property needs to be transferred to higher ground.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:45 AM EDT Monday the stage was 13.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:45 AM EDT Monday was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Friday afternoon and continue falling to 9.7 feet early Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Detailed river forecasts and additional information can be found at
www.weather.gov/iwx under Rivers and Lakes.

This statement will be updated within the next 12 to 24 hours.

Diegograndi Special Coverage / Global 21 September 2026 7 minutes Updates from the UN General Assembly 2026 Marking the opening of the 81st UN General Assembly, Crisis Group experts discuss challenges facing the UN’s efforts to promote international peace and security. This page includes updates from the High-Level Week in New York and recent Crisis Group coverage of the UN. Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Multilateral Diplomacy World leaders are gathering in New York during the week of 21 September for the UN General Assembly’s annual high-level session. They will find an organisation trapped in an open-ended institutional crisis. UN diplomacy to halt wars and ease civilian suffering is largely paralysed, while a second year of cost cutting has weakened the organisation’s capacity to respond. The UN is in need of revival. Even with these limitations, the UN remains the only universal forum for international cooperation on war and peace, even as the world order it anchors is under mounting strain. Many member states hope that the next Secretary-General, set to be selected by the end of 2026, can help the organisation forge a new direction that enhances diplomacy and deepens respect for international law. A new Secretary-General, regardless of the skills and experiences that she or he may bring to the role, cannot solve the world’s crises overnight. But she or he can and should work with member states to address immediate challenges. High on the list should be bolstering the UN’s peacemaking and conflict management capacities, mobilising political and financial support, and making a renewed case for international cooperation. This special coverage page will feature all of Crisis Group’s work related to the UN General Assembly’s High-Level Week in 2026, as well as its broader work on the UN from the past year. Our Experts on UNGA 21 Sep 2026 Guterres has certainly been very conservative and cautious on the UN’s role in peace and security. CNN Daniel Forti Head of UN Affairs 20 Sep 2026 The UN may not be in emergency care like it was last year, but it seems to be trapped in a trauma centre for the foreseeable future. Reuters Richard Gowan Program Director, Global Issues and Institutions 18 Sep 2026 China has long seen [UNGA] high-level week as U.S. turf. AFP Daniel Forti Head of UN Affairs 17 Sep 2026 This may be the worst time in the life of the UN, but it’s not the time to write an obituary. It’s diminished, but it’s not dead. The New Yorker Comfort Ero President & CEO 16 Sep 2026 As yet, there are no signs that Iran and the US will use the General Assembly as an opportunity for diplomacy to dial down their conflict. TRT World Richard Gowan Program Director, Global Issues and Institutions 15 Sep 2026 U.N. processes move considerably less rapidly than AI does … It isn’t clear that the next secretary-general will keep up this focus. AP Richard Gowan Program Director, Global Issues and Institutions For the latest updates from the UNGA High-level Week, follow our UN team on X: Richard Gowan , Daniel Forti and Mariea Sekijima . UNGA INSIGHTS In the run up to and during UNGA High-Level Week, Crisis Group will publish regular previews providing insight into upcoming events of interest at the UN, including brief comments from Crisis Group analysts. UN General Assembly Insights: Monday 21 September UN General Assembly Insights: Tuesday 22 September UN General Assembly Insights: Wednesday 23 September (to follow) UN General Assembly Insights: Thursday 24 September (to follow) UN General Assembly Insights: Friday 25 September (to follow) Our Recent Publications About the UN SPECIAL BRIEFING | Ten Challenges for the UN in 2026-2027 As the 2026 General Assembly begins, the UN remains hobbled by cost cutting and big-power wrangling. The new Secretary-General to be chosen soon cannot cure all that ails the organisation, but much can be done to put its still considerable capacity to work. Published 14 September 2026. Available here . External Publications by our Experts on the UN Shrink the UN By Richard Gowan, originally published in Foreign Affairs on 21 September 2026. General Assembly, Competition May Outdo Cooperation By Richard Gowan, Daniel Forti and Mariea Sekijima, originally published in Just Security on 17 September 2026. events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Guam. * WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Wednesday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Heavy rainfall from Invest 91W located south of Guam may lead to flash flooding Tuesday through Wednesday evening. Guidance shows 2 to 5 inches of rain falling during the watch period as Invest 91W moves just west of Guam. Many locations across Guam have already seen 2 to 4 inches of rain since Saturday and soils remain wet from heavy rainfall the last couple of weeks. This will allow for a lower threshold for flash flooding over the next couple of days. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central, northeast, southeast, and west central New Mexico, including the following areas, in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern Lincoln County, Estancia Valley, Lower Rio Grande Valley, Middle Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque Metro Area, San Agustin Plains and Adjacent Lowlands, Sandia and Manzano Mountains including Edgewood, South Central Highlands, South Central Mountains and Upper Tularosa Valley. In east central New Mexico, De Baca County and Guadalupe County. In north central New Mexico, East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley, Glorieta Mesa Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands, Santa Fe Metro Area and Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. In northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far Northeast Highlands, Harding County and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County. In west central New Mexico, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands and West Central Mountains. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive Tuesday and Wednesday with widespread heavy rain. Scattered occurrences of flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 2 inches in many locations along and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many locations westward to the continental divide. Stronger storms will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2 inches per hour, and storms will train repeatedly in succession over some locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching 4 to 6 inches over portions of central and eastern New Mexico. Heavy rain will likely continue Wednesday night over eastern areas, then showers and storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast to return along and east of the continental divide again on Thursday. - Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas, normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams. As the event unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of storms. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southwest New Mexico, including the following areas, Lowlands of the Bootheel, Southwest Desert/Lower Gila River Valley, Uplands of the Bootheel and Upper Gila River Valley. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An early season back door cool front will interact with a late season plume of deep tropical moisture, bringing several rounds of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Watch, one to two feet of inundation above ground level possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Atlantic Coastal Cape May, Coastal Atlantic and Coastal Ocean. * WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from Tuesday morning through Tuesday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 PM to 10 PM EDT Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday afternoon through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate tidal flooding could continue through at least Friday evening's high tide or perhaps longer.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop.

Be prepared to begin taking appropriate action to protect life
and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency
management officials. Be sure to check the latest forecast from
time to time in case a warning is issued or any new information
becomes available.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

deaths occur in vehicles.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of New Mexico, including the following areas,
Central Grant County/Silver City Area, East Central Tularosa
Basin/Alamogordo, East Slopes Sacramento Mountains Below 7500 Feet,
Eastern Black Range Foothills, Lowlands of the Bootheel, Northern
Dona Ana County, Otero Mesa, Sacramento Mountains Above 7500 Feet,
Sierra County Lakes, Southeast Tularosa Basin, Southern Dona Ana
County/Mesilla Valley, Southern Gila Foothills/Mimbres Valley,
Southern Gila Region Highlands/Black Range, Southwest Desert/Lower
Gila River Valley, Southwest Desert/Mimbres Basin, Uplands of the
Bootheel, Upper Gila River Valley, West Central Tularosa
Basin/White Sands and West Slopes Sacramento Mountains Below 7500
Feet and southwest Texas, including the following areas,
Eastern/Central El Paso County, Northern Hudspeth Highlands/Hueco
Mountains, Rio Grande Valley of Eastern El Paso/Western Hudspeth
Counties and Western El Paso County.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and
rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An early season back door cool front will interact with a late
season plume of deep tropical moisture, bringing several rounds
of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday
afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may
tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end
precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest
rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday
morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Illinois... Des Plaines River near Russell affecting Lake IL County. Des Plaines River near Gurnee affecting Lake IL County. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Des Plaines River from IL/WI state line downstream to US-41 in Gurnee, including the Russell gauge. * WHEN...Until late Saturday night. * IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Agricultural and park land is inundated near the river. Residential property is threatened near the river. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 6:30 PM CDT Monday the stage was 8.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected remain near 8.7 feet tonight then gradually fall Tuesday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Saturday evening. - Flood stage is 7.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Lake, IL

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued September 21 at 7:17PM CDT until September 27 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Chicago IL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Illinois...

Des Plaines River near Russell affecting Lake IL County.

Des Plaines River near Gurnee affecting Lake IL County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Des Plaines River from IL/WI state line downstream to US-41
in Gurnee, including the Russell gauge.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Agricultural and park land is inundated near
the river. Residential property is threatened near the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM CDT Monday the stage was 8.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected remain near 8.7 feet tonight
then gradually fall Tuesday morning. It will then fall below
flood stage Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or
may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

These forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as
forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by Tuesday afternoon.
weather.areaDesc: Lake, IL

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central, northeast, southeast, and west central New Mexico, including the following areas, in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern Lincoln County, Estancia Valley, Lower Rio Grande Valley, Middle Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque Metro Area, San Agustin Plains and Adjacent Lowlands, Sandia and Manzano Mountains including Edgewood, South Central Highlands, South Central Mountains and Upper Tularosa Valley. In east central New Mexico, De Baca County and Guadalupe County. In north central New Mexico, East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley, Glorieta Mesa Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands, Santa Fe Metro Area and Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. In northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far Northeast Highlands, Harding County and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County. In west central New Mexico, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands and West Central Mountains. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive Tuesday and Wednesday with widespread heavy rain. Scattered occurrences of flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 2 inches in many locations along and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many locations westward to the continental divide. Stronger storms will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2 inches per hour, and storms will train repeatedly in succession over some locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching 4 to 6 inches over portions of central and eastern New Mexico. Heavy rain will likely continue Wednesday night over eastern areas, then showers and storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast to return along and east of the continental divide again on Thursday. - Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas, normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams. As the event unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of storms. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 12 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Watch, one to two feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Atlantic Coastal Cape May, Coastal Atlantic and Coastal Ocean. * WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from Tuesday morning through Friday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 PM to 10 PM EDT Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 8 AM Wednesday to 6 PM EDT Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday afternoon through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS....Significant beach erosion is likely through this week and into the weekend. Moderate tidal flooding could continue through Friday or perhaps longer.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...All of south-central and southwestern New Mexico, as well as El Paso and western Hudspeth Counties in Texas. The area of greatest concern will be near and east of the Continental Divide to the Tularosa Basin and Sacramento Mountains. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An early season back door cool front will interact with a late season plume of deep tropical moisture, bringing several rounds of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.description: * WHAT...2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Areas along the beaches of the Outer Banks, especially on Hatteras and Ocraoke Island. * WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Friday evening. Most significant impacts expected during the Thursday evening and Friday morning high tide cycles. * IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Some roads and low lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding. Vulnerable areas along Highway 12 on Ocracoke and Hatteras Island are especially at risk for inundation from the oceanside.

In north central New Mexico, East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley, Glorieta Mesa Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands, Santa Fe Metro Area and Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. In northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far Northeast Highlands, Harding County and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County. In west central New Mexico, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands and West Central Mountains. * WHEN...From noon MDT today through Wednesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive today and Wednesday with widespread heavy rain. Scattered occurrences of flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 1.5 inches many locations along and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many locations westward to around Dulce, Gallup, and Glenwood. Stronger storms will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2 inches per hour, and storms will train repeatedly in succession over some locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching over 4 inches over portions of southern, central, and eastern New Mexico. Heavy rain will likely continue Wednesday night over north-central and eastern New Mexico, then showers and storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast to return to much of the state again on Thursday. - Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas, normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams. As the event unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of storms. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 22 at 2:47AM EDT until September 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...Today and again on Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Life-threatening rip currents are likely for all
people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches
should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The high rip current risk likely persists
through late week.
weather.instruction:
If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Watch, 2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Northern Outer Banks and Hatteras Island. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this evening. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday afternoon through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding may extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and businesses. Some roads and low lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding. Vulnerable areas along Highway 12 on Ocracoke and Hatteras Island are especially at risk for inundation from the oceanside. Dangerous rip currents. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide, which will occur around 10:00 AM today.

miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Conditions have generally tapered down across Majuro from yesterdays wind and rain event. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will bring some locally heavy showers through tonight. Further north, a tropical disturbance has produced robust convection across Bikini Atoll and the far northern Marshall Islands today. This morning's scatterometer shows that gusts could be approaching 40 to 45 knots in the heaviest showers and thunderstorms. Some of this heavy weather has made it as far south of Kwajalein today. Over the next couple of days, model guidance shows a westward shift of the tropical disturbance with a slow weakening trend. Scattered showers will remain possible across the RMI this week with a monsoon-like pattern remaining in place. Seas could approach 9 to 12 feet where the strongest winds and heaviest showers occur. This would make conditions hazardous to Small Craft across the far northern RMI with extreme choppiness. Boaters moving through the Marshall Islands north of Kwajalein should practice enhanced caution over the next day or so. For more information keep up to date with the latest information from the Majuro Weather Service office and your local emergency management agency.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: An active monsoon pattern will continue across western Micronesia with satellite imagery continuing to show areas of heavy showers and thunderstorms. Latest satellite-dervied surface wind data depicts 15 to 20 mph west to southwest winds across western Yap State and Palau with pockets of locally higher winds. Weather models point to a continuation of these conditions with periods of locally heavy showers moving across the islands, occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts, and choppy seas. Both Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of Invest 91W, located near 13N142E, northeast of Yap. 91W is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center and showers are expected to remain mostly numerous to widespread and heavy at times. Model guidance suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain per day will be possible through Wednesday, especially for Yap. Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any marine advisories that may be issued over the next couple of days. Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your local Weather Service Office.

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: AQAHGX The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for Wednesday, September 23, 2026. Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and surrounding areas on Wednesday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work, avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle properly tuned. events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Statement, up to one half foot of inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. * WHERE...Southern Nassau County. * WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday evening. For the Coastal Flood Statement, from Wednesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. * IMPACTS...Brief minor flooding of the more vulnerable locations near the waterfront and shoreline. Life- threatening rip currents are likely for all people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The high rip current risk is expected to persist through late week.

location.region: Southern Nassau

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 22 at 3:19PM EDT until September 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Statement, up to one half foot of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Southern Nassau County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Statement, from Wednesday
afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Brief minor flooding of the more vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline. Life-
threatening rip currents are likely for all people entering
the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches should stay out of
the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The high rip current risk is expected to
persist through late week.
weather.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...All of south-central and southwestern New Mexico, as well as El Paso and western Hudspeth Counties in Texas. The area of greatest concern will be near and east of the Continental Divide to the Tularosa Basin and Sacramento Mountains. * WHEN...Through Wednesday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An early season back door cold front will interact with a late season plume of deep tropical moisture, bringing several rounds of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region this afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest rain potential will likely be tonight into Wednesday morning. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: We are currently tracking a low that is expected to move through the southern Bering Sea Thursday through Saturday and which could approach the coast of the Yukon Delta. While the most likely storm track south of our area would result in only modest rises in above normal high water for the Yukon Delta, a further north track could result in high surf potential. As of right now, the southern portion of the Yukon Delta coast could see water levels rise to around 1 to 3 feet above the mean high water line, with rises more likely to be on the lower side of that range. We will continue to monitor this system closely.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Water levels on average of 1 to 2 feet above the normal highest tide line. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected Thursday. South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts to 50 mph expected Friday. * WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast including Kwigillingok and Kipnuk. * WHEN...From 4 AM Thursday to 4 AM Saturday. * IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be multiple peaks in water levels for the Kuskokwim Delta Thursday morning through Saturday morning coinciding with high tide cycles and strong southerly winds. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts to 60 mph Thursday afternoon will diminish early Friday until the low pressure system moves west of the coast by Friday afternoon. Then, winds will become southerly at 30 to 40 mph with gusts to 50 mph by Friday afternoon. Winds gradually weaken but remain southerly through Saturday. For Kwigillingok, water levels reach 1 to 2 feet above the normal highest tide line on Thursday, coinciding with the passage of a frontal system. Water levels could reach up to 4 feet in a worst case scenario. For Kipnuk, the highest water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the normal highest tide line are expected on Friday as a low pressure system moves west of the coast and winds become southerly. Water levels could reach 2 to 3 feet in a worst case scenario. For more information regarding potential local flood impacts, please reference maps.dggs.alaska.gov/akfit/

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Interior Kuskokwim Delta, including Kwethluk, Kasigluk, Bethel, Napaskiak, Napakiak, Oscarville, and other nearby villages. * WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive rain in combination of persistent high water levels and storm surge may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood with more heavy rain. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A strong storm projected to move into the eastern Bering Sea will bring heavy rainfall and storm surge to the area. The Kuskokwim River is currently running high, with statistics showing the river is already above the 90th percentile in flow for this time of year. 1 to 2 inches of rainfall across the Kilbuck Mountains, as well as across the lower Kuskokwim, is likely to exacerbate high water levels for the Kwethluk River, Johnson River / tundra villages, as well as other smaller tributaries and sloughs of the Kuskokwim. Confidence is moderate-to-high that flooding of low-lying areas will occur for Kwethluk and Kasigluk, where high-water was reported last week. Confidence is lower for flooding elsewhere and will be dependent on the rainfall amount and degree of compounding effects from coastal surge and tide cycle. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

flooded. Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood
with more heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A strong storm projected to move into the eastern Bering Sea will
bring heavy rainfall and storm surge to the area. The Kuskokwim
River is currently running high, with statistics showing the
river is already above the 90th percentile in flow for this time
of year. 1 to 2 inches of rainfall across the Kilbuck Mountains,
as well as across the lower Kuskokwim, is likely to exacerbate
high water levels for the Kwethluk River, Johnson River / tundra
villages, as well as other smaller tributaries and sloughs of the
Kuskokwim.

Confidence is moderate-to-high that flooding of low-lying areas
will occur for Kwethluk and Kasigluk, where high-water was
reported last week. Confidence is lower for flooding elsewhere
and will be dependent on the rainfall amount and degree of
compounding effects from coastal surge and tide cycle.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves expected, and strong longshore currents in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...East Carteret County. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Wednesday morning through Wednesday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 2 PM Wednesday to 11 AM EDT Friday. * IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in a low threat of property damage along the Neuse River. Some roads and low lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* WHAT...For the first Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip
currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves
peaking at 10 to 15 feet expected in the surf zone. For the
second Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents and large
breaking waves north of Cape Hatteras. Dangerous rip currents,
large breaking waves, and strong longshore currents in the surf
zone south of Cape Hatteras. For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2
to 4 feet of inundation above ground level expected in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Up to 1 foot of
inundation is possible for sound-side flooding from Buxton
southward when winds become more northerly late Thursday and
Friday.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the first Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT
this evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM Wednesday
to 8 PM EDT Saturday. For the second Beach Hazards Statement,
from Wednesday morning through Wednesday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 PM Wednesday to 11 PM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Portions of Highway 12
will be inundated. Low lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from
shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a
swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and
back injuries. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Prolonged nature of the event will continue
to erode dune structures. Winds and waves are forecast to peak
latter half of Thursday.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.
weather.areaDesc: Hatteras Island

events.title: Flash Flood Warning
events.description: FFWFGZ The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... Navajo County in north central Arizona... * Until 900 PM MST /1000 PM MDT/. * At 604 PM MST /704 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area, southeast of Indian Wells. Between 0.75 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.75 to 1.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing flash flooding. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Twin Buttes. This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers... Pueblo Colorado Wash, Steamboat Wash, Bidahochi Wash and Leroux Wash.

location.region: Navajo, AZ

weather.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 22 at 6:04PM MST until September 22 at 9:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
weather.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* Until 900 PM MST /1000 PM MDT/.

* At 604 PM MST /704 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area, southeast of Indian
Wells. Between 0.75 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts of 0.75 to 1.5 inches are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Twin Buttes.

Pueblo Colorado Wash, Steamboat Wash, Bidahochi Wash and Leroux
Wash.
weather.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy Counties. .The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau. The hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water levels to rise. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and is forecast to continue. * WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river in Citrus and Marion counties. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:45 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 28.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to hold steady at flood stage. Additional rises are possible. - Flood stage is 28.2 feet. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2 feet on 10/02/1979. - https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued September 22 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and is forecast to continue.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to hold steady at flood stage.
Additional rises are possible.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 200 PM EDT.
weather.areaDesc: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL
